source_text: Filii igitur nec tunc rei sunt, quando in eorum generatione peccant parentes; quia in tantum ad liberos suos pertinent, in quantum parentes sunt; igitur et tantum filii ad parentes pertinent, in quantum filii sunt. Naturae quippe generantium constat germina communicare, non culpae. Quod si, ut ratio demonstrat, ita etiam Apostolum confirmare pronuntias; merito nos, eo docente, defendimus peccata parentum ad filios pertinere non posse; quandoquidem et Apostolus Spiritu Sancto clarus, et nos instructi luce rationis, et tu pondere impugnatae a te veritatis oppressus, communiter vereque fateamur, parentes in quantum parentes sunt, reos non esse; in tantum autem ad filios pertinere, in quantum parentes sunt; igitur filios in quantum filii sunt, id est, antequam aliquid per voluntatem propriam operentur, reos esse non posse.
pass_a_gloss: Children therefore are not even then defendants, when the parents sin in their generation; because they belong to their children only insofar as they are parents; therefore also children belong to parents only insofar as they are children. For it stands that the germs of those generating communicate nature, not guilt. Which if, as reason demonstrates, you also pronounce that the Apostle confirms; we meritedly, with him teaching, defend that the sins of parents cannot belong to children; seeing that both the Apostle, bright with the Holy Spirit, and we instructed by the light of reason, and you, oppressed by the weight of the truth attacked by you, commonly and truly confess that parents, insofar as they are parents, are not defendants; but belong to children only insofar as they are parents; therefore children, insofar as they are children, that is, before they work anything through their own will, cannot be defendants.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: Children, then, are not guilty even when their parents sin in begetting them. For parents are connected to their children only insofar as they are parents; correspondingly, children are connected to their parents only insofar as they are children. It is established that offspring share in their progenitors’ nature, not their fault. If you declare that the apostle confirms what reason demonstrates, then we rightly defend, under his instruction, the position that parents’ sins cannot belong to their children. The apostle, radiant with the Holy Spirit; we, instructed by reason’s light; and you, crushed by the weight of the truth you attack, all jointly and truly confess that parents, insofar as they are parents, are not guilty. They are connected to their children only insofar as they are parents. Consequently, children insofar as they are children—that is, before performing any act through their own will—cannot be guilty.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Parents insofar as parents are not guilty; keep the forensic 'in quantum parentes sunt'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
